=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5030-25157 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Every hold check on a PR labelled `ai:merge-lease-wait` calls `_stall_merge_lease_label_age_minutes` (lines 25050-25052, 25143-25146), which makes a new, uncached `gh_retry gh api graphql` timelineItems(LABELED_EVENT) read. The same PR can be read up to four times per stalled issue per tick (recover_stalled_issue lines 30271 and 30274, invoke_stall_judge line 24020, `_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard` line 5413). The helper header at line 25079 still says "Makes no API calls.", and caller comments (e.g. 22166, 22827, 28641, 29199, 30261-30271) still say "0 extra API calls".
  WHY: This runs in the per-issue stall loop on every poller tick for as long as the lease hold lasts (default 1440 min) and does not use STALL_MANAGED_LINKED_PR_CACHE / `_candidate_details_json`. That breaks the issue's "no per-iteration API calls in the poller loop" constraint and the §14 cache rule, and the stale comments will mislead future audits. All five reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:25050-25155 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The label-age query `timelineItems(itemTypes:[LABELED_EVENT],last:50)` sees only the 50 newest labeled events. If the current `ai:merge-lease-wait` labeled event is older than that, or the GraphQL read keeps failing, the helper returns no age and `_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason` keeps the hold with no upper bound (25099-25100).
  WHY: The issue can stay held past `STALL_MERGE_LEASE_WAIT_MAX_MINUTES`, which defeats the bounded-wait mitigation, and no test covers the overflow path. Severity disagreement: gemini and minimax rated MAJOR, luna and glm rated NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5247-5300 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr` builds `_sjp_order` (line 5268) as branch hits, then body close-keyword hits, then the remaining candidates, and returns the first implementation PR in that order. It does not pick the lowest-numbered passing PR from the sorted union that `close_linked_pr` iterates.
  WHY: With two open implementation PRs (e.g. #100 found only through the timeline, #200 through the branch lookup), the judge diagnostics, the `STALL_JUDGE_LINKED_PR` log and the source=judge_pick hold check describe a different PR from the one `close_linked_pr` reaches first. This contradicts issue #9892 step 1, the header comment and the agents.d text, and `test_stall_judge_pick_tries_branch_hits_before_many_cross_refs` locks the ordering in. Severity disagreement: gemini, minimax and glm rated MAJOR, claude and luna rated NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5474-5475 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The prefix assignment `PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS="${_srg_ids}" _pr_checks_completed ...` is said to stay set after the function returns, so later `_pr_checks_completed` calls (15957, 29380, 33293, 34072, 35408, 35472, 35811, 35905) would filter check-runs against stale run ids.
  WHY: A later merge gate on a different PR could read the required CI check as absent or unknown and block a mergeable PR. Severity disagreement: glm rated MAJOR, gemini rated NIT; the highest is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 checked this claim and dropped it, saying that in bash outside POSIX mode the assignment lasts only for that call (the script relies on this at lines 28971 and 30298).
- tests/test_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard.py:441-466 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The docstring of `test_guard_without_stall_clock_does_not_hold_lease_wait` says the review-blocked arm calls the guard without stall minutes. That arm now calls `_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard "${rb_issue}" "0"` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 36054) and does refuse on merge_lease_wait.
  WHY: Nothing breaks at runtime, but a maintainer who trusts the docstring could restore the one-argument call and bring back closing of lease-waiting PRs while the tests still pass. All three rated it NIT.
- agents.d/9892-stall-recovery-keeps-green-lease-waiting-prs.md:10 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In the `STALL_REISSUE_REFUSED` bullet, `|check_unavailable` sits outside the closing backtick, but `_stall_reissue_guard_refuse` (line 5387) does emit `reason=check_unavailable` (initialised at line 5369).
  WHY: A log parser that uses the documented format as a regex literal would miss the fail-closed `reason=check_unavailable` refusal lines.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5275-5300 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The picker is said to store each fetched payload in `_sjp_fetched_json[pr]` before checking that the fetch succeeded, so the `{}` failure sentinel would be reused by the cross_ref_last fallback as STALL_JUDGE_PICKED_PR_JSON.
  WHY: After a network error, invoke_stall_judge would skip the fresh fetch and the diagnostics fields would read as empty. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash checked this and say it is false: line 5276 runs `continue` on `{}` before the store at line 5277.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Reuse ... the existing commit-status lookups for the head check." (issue #9892 §Constraints, §Approach step 3)
  expected_change_site: `_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard` at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5416-5447 (status read block)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The guard makes a direct `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${_srg_sha}/statuses?per_page=100"` request (line 5426; luna cites 5424-5427, glm ~5417). No caller passes in a pre-fetched status payload, and the script has no shared status cache for `ai-review/head-gate` reads. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 does not count this as a gap, citing the issue's Risks section ("status/check lookups happen only on the rare close_and_reissue path").
- requirement: "The wait is measured from the label's last `labeled` event, which the issue timeline the stall path already fetches carries," and "Reuse the pulls/<n> payload already fetched ... for labels."
  expected_change_site: `_stall_merge_lease_label_age_minutes` at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:25030-25062 and its callers (the `_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason` label read)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: `_stall_merge_lease_label_age_minutes` makes a separate `gh_retry gh api graphql` request for `pullRequest.timelineItems` at lines 25050-25052 and does not use the timeline data the stall path already fetched; no fetched payload is passed in. It issues a fresh `timelineItems(LABELED_EVENT,last:50)` call per held PR per tick, which breaks the "no per-iteration API calls in the poller loop" constraint. glm adds that the reuse requirement is only partly met: the PR payload and `_pr_checks_completed` are reused, but the statuses and label-timestamp reads are new.
- requirement: "Returns the first open PR from `_find_all_linked_prs` that passes `_linked_pr_is_issue_implementation` (lowest number first, matching how `close_linked_pr` iterates)." (issue #9892 §Approach step 1)
  expected_change_site: `_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr` at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5247-5300
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The helper builds the fetch order as `branch hits → body hits → all candidates` (deduped), returns the first passing PR in that order, and does not sort ascending. `close_linked_pr` iterates the sorted union. `test_stall_judge_pick_tries_branch_hits_before_many_cross_refs` codifies the branch-first design.
- requirement: "Done when: the new tests pass; the orchestrator suite passes" and the accepted plan's `check | lint` acceptance row (issue #9892 done-check table)
  expected_change_site: PR-level verification (shellcheck of scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh; tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py)
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The PR description's pre-push gate lists `shellcheck` under "Failures caused by this change" in both the implement run and the last repair run, marks the `check | lint` row "not run", and marks `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` unverified (timeout). The failure is unmapped (no file:line; local shellcheck 0.9.0 OOM, CI pins 0.10, and PR check-runs show failed_count 0 for head 9c72e9f).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr, the _sjp_order build (about line 5268) and the loop `done <<< "${_sjp_order}"` (about line 5291) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Branch and body close-keyword hits are tried before the ascending candidates, so the pick is no longer the lowest-numbered open implementation PR (#100 found only through the timeline vs #200 found through `ai/issue-<n>`). This contradicts the header comment, the agents.d fragment and the issue spec.
  WHY: The diagnostics `linked_pr` and the source=judge_pick hold check describe a different PR from the first one close_linked_pr (line 20206) reaches. The damage is limited to which PR the judge sees, and only with two or more open implementation PRs. Fix: keep scanning the lower-numbered candidates already fetched, or correct the comments.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason lease branch calling _stall_merge_lease_label_age_minutes (about lines 25143-25146); recover_stalled_issue lines 30271 and 30274; invoke_stall_judge line 24020; _stall_reissue_green_pr_guard line 5413 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Every hold check on a PR labelled `ai:merge-lease-wait` makes an uncached `gh_retry gh api graphql` timelineItems(LABELED_EVENT) read inside the per-issue stall loop (line 36929), up to four reads per stalled issue per tick. The comment at lines 30261-30267 still says "(0 extra API calls)", and the header at line 25079 still says "Makes no API calls."
  WHY: This costs one to four extra GraphQL requests per lease-labelled stalled issue per tick and conflicts with "no per-iteration API calls in the poller loop" and the §14 cache rule. Fix: cache the age per PR for the poller process (e.g. in a mktemp key file like _STALL_MERGE_LEASE_LAPSE_LOG_FILE) and correct the comments.
- tests/test_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard.py:docstring of test_guard_without_stall_clock_does_not_hold_lease_wait | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docstring says the review-blocked arm calls the guard without stall minutes, but that arm now calls `_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard "${rb_issue}" "0"` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 36054) and refuses on merge_lease_wait.
  WHY: A maintainer could restore the one-argument call and bring back closing of lease-waiting PRs while the test still passes. Reword it.
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: NONE. All three approach steps, the tests, README, env wiring, changelog, agents.d and LOG_PREFIX entries are present. The fresh statuses read is covered by the issue's Risks section; the other `_issue_cross_ref_pr_number_last` call sites are an explicit non-goal.
